name: Physlib Formalisation Report: Thermodynamics of the canonical ensemble and the fluctuation–dissipation theorem
description: Physlib Contribution Report on work by Matteo Cipollina: “Thermodynamics of the canonical ensemble and the fluctuation–dissipation theorem”.

issuer.name: Physlib Contributions
issuer.description: An open-source community project to digitalize results from physics into Lean 4. Physlib Contributions publishes signed reports on reviewing, maintenance, refactoring, foundations, formalisation and documentation of Physlib.

credentialSubject.narrative: Extended the canonical ensemble in Physlib from its basic definitions to the main thermodynamic results. Added a semi-classical normalisation, with a phase-space unit and a number of degrees of freedom, so that the partition function, Helmholtz free energy and thermodynamic entropy are dimensionless physical quantities, kept alongside their raw mathematical versions. Proved the identity F = U − TS, the mean energy as U = −∂ log Z/∂β, the relation between thermodynamic and differential entropy, and, for finite systems, that the thermodynamic entropy equals the Shannon entropy. Defined energy variance and heat capacity, and proved the fluctuation–dissipation theorem C_V = Var(E)/(k_B T²) for finite canonical ensembles. Made Temperature a structure and added the conversions, limits and derivatives in temperature that these results need.

achievement.name: Physlib Formalisation Report
achievement.description: For adding to Physlib or PhyslibAlpha: new lemmas and definitions, and results from physics stated and proved on top of what is already there. This includes many small additions across different areas, as well as one larger result.

criteria.narrative:
- The work added new lemmas, definitions or results to Physlib or PhyslibAlpha, rather than restructuring existing code or setting up the basic definitions of an area.
- The work was merged and follows the library’s conventions.
- Links to the relevant pull requests are given as evidence.
